column1: # Game profile of Monster Hunter Rise (Switch, base game cartridge dump v0 + update 16.0.2 = v2228224, Sunbreak included)
# Capcom's RE Engine on SDK 11.4.3 (the same sdk / subsdk0 builds as Metroid Dread and 13 Sentinels), NVN. Everything lives in RE Engine PAK archives (re_chunk_000.pak + 16 patches, 19.6 GB, KPKA v4,
# zstd / deflate entries); the shaders are its SDF definitions inside them (shader_split.py kpka_jobs / sdf_shaders: 63,111 shaders, 102,345 vertex / pixel pairs). main is 314 MB (125 MB of text),
# so the rewriter puts its patch area right before the base (patch_nso.py BIG_TEXT). The GPU heap is one 64 GB sparse virtual memory pool (hle_nvn.c vpool_*)
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base game's control data, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID
# a 3D action game: camera on the right stick, item bar on the D-pad
# only the merged 16.0.2 copy is extracted
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie 11.4.3: the opening movies are H.264 into an NVN texture with AAC 5.1 sound)
# RE Engine fills small textures from the CPU in place (the menu cursor's 8 × 8 BC1 texture: 32 bytes written into a CPU-visible pool, no packaged layout, no WriteTexels), so they must be uploaded
# from guest memory (without these keys the cursor highlight composited black on black and the menus looked frozen)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host raises RE Engine's frame limit from 30 to 60 (hle_fpslock.c, FPSLocker's address for this build); the game still asks for present interval 2,
# which display mode ignores. The game steps by the time that really passed. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps 30 and saves power

# The NPDM declares no system resource, so there is no virtual address memory: the game sizes its heap as pool − used memory with SetHeapSize. 4 GB block: 256 MB alias, 256 MB stacks, 3.25 GB heap region
# SetHeapSize asked for the pool − 64 MB − bss (0xc9000000) with the default, but the loaded modules take 0x13fa4000 (main alone 314 MB of text + ro + data), so the request failed at boot:
# used memory must cover them, as on hardware. With 328 MB the heap is 2.88 GB
